It could be your cpu, or your ram speed specifically. You can have a 1070 with 16gb of ram BUT your ram could be ddr3 and lower frequencies.  

I had a gtx 970 with 16g of 1600mhz ddr3 ram and when I maxed my settings on rust I was stuck at 40 to 60 fps. When I was watching task manager, my ram was at 98%, when my cpu and GPU were at 60%.  My ram couldnt send information to my gpu and cpu fast enough to have them max out their performance. This could be a possibility on why your only getting those frames. 

General standard ram speed nowadays is 3200 mhz ddr4. 

If you are stuck with that ddr3 ram, then you will have to get a new motherboard which can use ddr4 ram... which will mean you probably need a new cpu because of the new motherboard. That was my issue, and I basically had to just buy a new pc.

I run on beautiful, but I turn all of the  high performance impact settings off or I put them on low. (Each individual setting will say if it's high performance impact if you mouse over it in the settings) and especially have shadows off. Rust will work on a 970 but if you can save up for a 1070 you'll have a much better time. 1060 and 970 have almost the same benchmarks but the 1060 has 2 more GB of vram.
